quotes.text: Some dude behind a desk –or an AI robot– shouldn't decide if you get the care your doctor prescribed. It's time to ban prior authorization policies. Now.
There is no place in our democracy for AI deepfakes

Today, you might see a TV ad starring something that... kind of looks like me.

My opponent's super PAC is using an AI deepfake of me to mislead voters. They can't win with the truth - so they're resorting to lies. 

It's disgusting. Minnesotans deserve better.

Donald Trump and his MAGA Republican buddies have completely eroded our faith in public institutions.

There's no room for AI deepfakes in our politics. https://t.co/QFRjIBpxit

Dark money supergroups have already spent $11 million for my opponent. 

AIPAC, crypto, an AI billionaire, and health insurance companies are supporting Congresswoman Craig because her record shows that she will support what they want. https://t.co/bUgiSLzPgQ

I mean, I think we have to be incredibly cautious when it comes to artificial intelligence and AI. [...] I'm also really worried about what this means for the workforce. If we see AI taking individuals' jobs away, I think it's important that those corporations then have to pay a price for it. you know, either through, you know, taxes or other means.

We have to be able to keep up with technology. But my worry is that the technology is going to exceed the guardrails that we have in place right now. We have to ensure that there are additional ones in place.

Your doctor should decide what care you need - not a dude behind a desk or worse, an AI robot.

It's time to ban prior authorization. https://t.co/irnnamPsGG

People across Minnesota are telling us they are freaked out about these massive, out-of-control data-center projects and Michele Tafoya's response to folks is to just accept it and plant trees around them so they're not an eyesore. I have a different take: Communities get to call the shots. Minnesotans decide, when, where and if data centers get built.

When we hear about young people who have died by suicide because of the conversations with these chatbots, I can't even believe that this is something where we are still questioning whether they should be regulated.

We are going to get rid of prior authorizations so that some dude behind a desk, or worse yet an AI bot, can't determine whether or not you get the life-saving healthcare that your doctor has prescribed.
